questions.question: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they must certify:

options.text: That the package does not contain hazardous materials.
That the package follows all rules.
That the package was packed at a different location.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the package follows all rules.
questions.explanation: A shipper of hazardous materials must certify on the shipping paper that the shipment follows all rules.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, a shipper should warn others by:

options.text: Displaying hazmat placards on their truck.
Using flashing lights on their truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Displaying hazmat placards on their truck.
questions.explanation: Shippers of hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs called placards on their vehicles. Shippers must also provide labels, shipping papers, and emergency response information.

questions.question: A placard must be placed:

options.text: At least three inches away from any other markings.
Under a ladder if space is limited.
On a background the same color as the placard.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least three inches away from any other markings.
questions.explanation: A placard must be at least three inches away from any other markings. Keep it clear of doors, ladders, and other attachments. Always place placards on a background with a contrasting color.

questions.question: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a shipping paper, which placard must be displayed?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on the shipping paper or package, you must display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard as appropriate.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Keep hazardous materials away from heat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a hook.
questions.explanation: Set the parking brake before loading or unloading hazardous materials. Do not use hooks or tools that could damage containers. Keep hazardous materials away from heat.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials cannot be transported in a trailer with:
questions.correctAnswerText: A heater.
questions.explanation: Cargo heaters are not allowed when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gases), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials in the same space.

questions.question: What shape are hazmat placards that show what materials are in a vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: A diamond
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: The National Response Center must be notified of an incident involving all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Injury not requiring hospitalization.
questions.explanation: Report incidents to the National Response Center if they result in death, hospitalization, $50,000 or more in property damage, evacuation of the public, or closure of a major transportation route for more than one hour. Also report fire, spillage, or contamination involving radiation, bacteria, or toxins.

questions.question: If a hazardous materials package is too small for a label, it should be labeled with:

options.text: Placement in a specific part of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: A tag.
questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials label will not fit on a package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be:

options.text: Inside a gas station looking through a window.
In the vehicle, awake or asleep.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 100 feet of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be awake inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. They must know the hazards, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the vehicle if necessary.

questions.question: When transporting chlorine, what must you do at a railroad crossing?

options.text: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
You must slow down before crossing the tracks.
You can cross if no warning lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: When transporting chlorine, you must always stop at a railroad crossing. Stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track. Do this even if you don't see a train.

questions.question: Your hazardous materials cargo catches fire. What should you do?

options.text: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
Keep driving to the fire department.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials fires need special training and equipment to fight safely. Unless you have this training, call 911 and let emergency workers handle it.

questions.question: What might show that cargo contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo comes from a supermarket.
The cargo is on wooden pallets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often hold hazardous materials. Use proper safety steps when transporting these items.

questions.question: You notice hazardous materials leaking from your vehicle while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving to find a phone and call for help.
Leave the vehicle to find help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Park your vehicle right away if cargo is leaking. Keep driving spreads contamination over a larger area, creating more danger and higher cleanup costs.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials placards?
questions.correctAnswerText: Diamonds.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: In an accident with hazardous materials, which is NOT your job as the driver?

options.text: Keep people away from the scene.
Try to put out the fire yourself.
Tell emergency workers about the hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to put out the fire yourself.
questions.explanation: Your jobs are to keep people away, stop the material from spreading if safe, tell emergency workers about the hazards, and give them shipping papers. Do not fight the fire unless you have training and protective gear.

questions.question: Hazardous cargo is leaking and you have no phone. What should you do?

options.text: Drive to a phone to call for help.
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility.
Send someone else to get help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Send someone else to get help.
questions.explanation: Do not move your vehicle more than needed. Continued driving spreads contamination. Park the vehicle, secure it, stay with it, and contact emergency personnel. If you don't have a phone, send someone else for help.

questions.question: To choose the right placard, what do you need to know?

options.text: The hazard class of the materials.
The type of container holding the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard class of the materials.
questions.explanation: Choose placards based on the hazard class, the amount of materials, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in your vehicle.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine must be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Off.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. You can only leave it running if you need the engine to operate a pump.

questions.question: Where should shipping papers be kept?

options.text: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in another place where you can reach them while wearing your seat belt. They must be visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: A driver should make sure that:

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare package markings and labels to the shipping papers. The shipper must show the correct basic description on the shipping paper and put the proper labels on the packages.

questions.question: A hazardous materials placard must be placed:

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the outside of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Opened.
questions.explanation: On a compressed gas tank, liquid discharge valves must be opened during loading and unloading. They should be closed at all other times.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials is to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Attend hazardous materials training courses.
questions.explanation: The manual is just the first step. You should also read federal and state rules about transporting hazardous materials. Attending hazardous materials training courses will help you learn more.

questions.question: To transport hazardous materials, a driver needs:

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
A CDL with a tank endorsement
A CDL with a cargo endorsement

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that transports hazardous materials.

questions.question: A placarded vehicle's engine must have a fire extinguisher with a minimum rating of:
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle's engine must have a fire extinguisher rated 10 B:C or higher by Underwriters Laboratories (UL).

questions.question: Hazardous materials shipping papers may be:

options.text: Kept in a pouch attached to the driver's side door.
Taped to the passenger's side window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Kept in a pouch attached to the driver's side door.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in another place where you can reach them easily while wearing your seat belt. The papers must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, you must park no closer than ____ from the nearest building.
questions.correctAnswerText: 300 feet
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Exception: you may park closer for a short time if you need to refuel or perform another necessary task.

questions.question: Unless a package is clearly unsafe, a driver needs ____ to accept it.
questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper's certification
questions.explanation: The shipper certifies that the package has been prepared according to Hazardous Materials Regulations. You may accept the shipper's certification unless the package is clearly unsafe or does not follow regulations.

questions.question: A person should not smoke within ____ of a vehicle placarded for Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials.
questions.correctAnswerText: 25 feet
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded cargo tank carrying Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (gases). Never smoke or carry a lit cigar, pipe, or cigarette near vehicles with flammable or explosive materials.
